newsitem.title: CHILE: Peirano said in talks to buy Santa Isabel.
newsitem.headline: Peirano said in talks to buy Santa Isabel.

text.p: Sources at Argentine supermarket chain Disco SA have confirmed that the chain's owner Juan Peirano and Argentina's Banco Velox are negotiating to buy Chile's Santa Isabel SA, a newspaper reported on Thursday.
Santiago paper El Mercurio reported that sources on the board of Disco have confirmed that Peirano, an Uruguayan businessman, has been negotiating to buy the supermarket chain.
The report quoted Disco director Carlos Pasianotti as saying that Disco was not buying Santa Isabel, but rather that Peirano was negotiating for the purchase through Banco Velox.

Santa Isabel said Wednesday its controlling shareholder and former general manager Eduardo Elberg received an offer from an independent investor to buy 36.96 percent of the chain, based in the Chilean city of Valparaiso.
An earlier report in El Mercurio, on Wednesday, said Peirano, who leads a business conglomerate that includes Disco and Banco Velox, had offered to buy about 30 percent of Santa Isabel.
Thursday's report added that negotiations had been confirmed from the Argentine side, adding that the purchase price was still unknown.
Since Wednesday was a market holiday in Chile, an official announcement would be made Thursday, Santa Isabel's statement said. The company has stores in Chile, Peru and Paraguay.
